parts.name: Two-stage HP and five-stage LP turbine

steps.title: Whole engine
steps.body: A two-spool, high-bypass turbofan. Air enters through the inlet lip on the left and is split by the fan: the outer stream leaves through the bypass nozzle, the inner stream runs through the compressor, the combustor and the turbine before leaving through the core nozzle. Roughly eight of every ten kilograms of air bypass the core, and that bypass stream produces most of the thrust.

steps.title: Inlet and fan
steps.body: The inlet lip is a thin rounded ring; the throat behind it is lined with acoustic panels that absorb fan noise before it leaves the engine. Twenty-two wide-chord titanium blades carry the fan. Their stagger angle falls from about 58° at the root to 27° at the tip, which keeps the tip speed supersonic only at the outer edge and gives the blade its wide, twisted shape. Each blade weighs as little as 150 g despite being roughly the size of a person.

steps.title: Nacelle and reverser
steps.body: The nacelle is the aerodynamic fairing around the fan. It forms the outer wall of the bypass duct and, on a real engine, carries the thrust reverser: the two trim lines on the fan cowl mark the sleeve that slides aft and exposes the cascade grilles, turning bypass air forward to brake the aircraft. The nacelle also picks up the engine load and hands it to the pylon.

steps.title: Core engine: axial compressor
steps.body: Behind the fan, the core starts with a three-stage booster on the low-pressure spool, then hands the air to an eight-stage high-pressure compressor. Rotor rows spin while stator rows stay bolted to the casing; each pair adds pressure and removes swirl. By the last stage the air is roughly 30 times atmospheric pressure and about 600 K, and the annulus has narrowed to a fraction of its original height.

steps.title: Annular combustor
steps.body: Twenty fuel nozzles feed a single annular flame tube. The liner is a double skin: the inner surface burns at over 1,800 K while cooling air, bled from the compressor, flows between the skins and enters through thousands of small holes to keep the metal below its melting point. Because the combustor is annular rather than a ring of separate cans, the engine stays short and the pressure loss stays low.

steps.title: Turbine and exhaust
steps.body: The gas leaving the combustor drives two turbine stages on the high-pressure spool, then five more on the low-pressure spool. The HP turbine turns the compressor it sits beside; the LP turbine turns the fan through a shaft that runs down the centre of the engine. Downstream the flow accelerates through the core nozzle past the exhaust plug, which fairings the last turbine stage and reduces base drag.

steps.title: Pylon and installation
steps.body: The pylon carries thrust and weight between the engine and the wing, and routes fuel, oil, hydraulic and bleed-air lines. Two mount links tie the fan case into the pylon: a forward mount that takes thrust and vertical load, and an aft mount that lets the case grow as it heats up. The accessory gearbox under the fan case takes shaft power off the HP spool to drive the fuel pumps, the oil pumps and the generators.

steps.title: Final inspection
steps.body: After assembly the engine goes to test: fan balance, core vibration, oil pressure and exhaust-gas temperature are logged across the operating range, then the engine is borescoped through the compressor and turbine stages. Every fastener torque and lockwire is signed off against ATA chapter 72 before the engine is released to the wing.
